newsitem.title: CHINA: China to keep policy on foreign auto investment.
newsitem.headline: China to keep policy on foreign auto investment.

text.p: China will not change its policy towards foreign investors in its automobile industry despite concerns of domestic firms that they will be edged out, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

Foreign investors should not be worried by debate in China's auto sector about the role of foreign partners, the newspaper quoted Zhang Xiaoyu, director of the automobile department under the Ministry of Machine-building Industry, as saying.
"China's stance for international cooperation for the industry has not changed and policies remain consistent," Zhang was quoted as saying.
Many domestic car manufactureres had voiced concern that foreign companies had not given their Chinese partners enough say in product development, Zhang said.
"Some senior Chinese auto executives began questioning the need for foreign partners and the possibility of adverse effects from their participation," he said.

China was still seeking cooperation with foreign auto makers to help develop the domestic industry, he said but gave no details. "No one will interfere in operating or proposed foreign-funded projects," he said.
